source.title: On the impact of activation and normalization in obtaining isometric embeddings at initialization
source.authors: A. Joudaki; Hadi Daneshmand; F. Bach

record.tranche_reason: Reports SGD training-loss convergence for MLPs with different activations, but does not measure training classification error or test the listed recipes directly.
record.gate_note: The paper's main results concern representation isometry. Figure 7 reports training-loss curves relevant to optimization speed; cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation isometry and compares SGD training loss across activations in layer-normalized MLPs. These results do not test any listed version: Figure 7 varies activation rather than initialization, and normalization and initialization comparisons elsewhere measure isometry rather than training speed or trainable depth.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Section 6.3: greater activation isometry strength correlates with faster SGD convergence in shallow layer-normalized MLPs, but the authors say the correlation does not extend to deeper networks. The paper's main conclusion concerns normalization and nonlinear activations promoting representation isometry, rather than demonstrated improvements in trainable depth.
record.recipe_differences: The study tracks training loss across activation functions in layer-normalized MLPs; it does not compare the claim's training recipes or measure classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that the convergence correlation appears in shallow networks, e.g., 10 layers or less, and does not extend to deeper networks.

fits_no_version.finding: At depth 10, width 1000 and batch size 512 on CIFAR-10, activations with greater isometry strength have faster SGD training-loss convergence, averaged over five runs. The authors state that this correlation does not extend to deeper networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation isometry strength correlates with SGD convergence speed in the tested shallow layer-normalized MLPs; the relationship does not extend to deeper networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The theory and experiments concern representation Gram-matrix isometry. Appendix B.2 reports improved isometry for mean-field centering and normalization compared with Xavier initialization, without comparing training speed or trainable depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization, activation and gain choices affect representation isometry at initialization in the tested MLPs.

record.problems: The convergence evidence is shown as a figure without numeric loss values. The paper states the correlation does not extend to deeper networks but gives no corresponding deeper-network training-loss result in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CNNs, including random or corrupted labels, and the effects of size, early stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with convolutional-network depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and training deep networks with special initialization or Fixup.

Effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, and comparisons of orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization. Appendix B.2 compares initialization-related choices only through representation isometry.
Loss recovery, curvature changes and divergence around the initial stability limit, and longer-term edge-of-stability dynamics.
Training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with versus without batch normalization, and normalization-free training using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Representation Gram-matrix isometry is distinct from controlling gradient propagation or establishing faster training through initialization. The deeper-network qualification concerns the activation-isometry correlation and does not itself challenge V3 or V4.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report training classification error or test network size, random/corrupted labels, early stopping, or regularized recipes.
Does not study teacher-student networks, spurious minima, or width relative to teacher size.
Does not compare plain and residual networks or measure training classification error across depth.
Does not compare initialization schemes or test whether activation-matched or orthogonal initialization increases trainable depth.
Does not vary learning rate around a stability limit or measure curvature and divergence.
Does not compare training speed with and without batch normalization or test Fixup.

rows.subject: MLP
rows.operation_detail: SGD training with different activation functions; training loss tracked by epoch.
rows.note: The text says convergence is faster for activations with significantly larger isometry strength in shallow MLPs, e.g., with 10 layers or less. No numeric loss values are stated.
rows.check: The qualitative convergence-speed finding is supported by Section 6.3, but it cannot establish any listed version. Replace the unspecified baseline with the other activation conditions. The row combines three activation conditions; separate them if recording individual curves. Numeric loss values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
